title: Mario Party 4
subtitle: A new console around the same party table
summary: Mario Party 4 is Hudson Soft's first GameCube entry in Nintendo's board-game series, released in North America on 21 October 2002.
body: Mario Party 4 is Hudson Soft's first GameCube entry in Nintendo's board-game series, released in North America on 21 October 2002. Four characters travel through themed boards, gathering coins and competing for Stars. A minigame after each round changes the balance before the next set of dice rolls. The familiar mixture gives a group several ways to influence the result: a useful item, a fortunate board event or a strong performance in a short challenge can each alter what the next turn makes possible.

Mega and Mini Mushrooms make size part of navigating the board. Growing larger provides extra movement and lets a character take coins from opponents passed along the route. Shrinking restricts the dice but opens small pipes and shortcuts. The choice is therefore tied to the current destination: moving farther is useful only if the route still leads somewhere worth reaching. Shops and other items add further ways to approach a Star or disturb another player's plan, keeping the board's social contest active between minigames.

The minigames divide the group into free-for-all, paired or uneven teams, sometimes turning an opponent from the board into a temporary partner. Booksquirm asks players to avoid being crushed by falling pages, while Dungeon Duos makes cooperation essential to moving through an obstacle course. Practice opportunities let a group learn a challenge before its scored attempt. Ichiro Shimakura composed the music. The GameCube debut keeps the gathering readable through bright themed spaces and brief changes of activity, with the next round returning every rivalry to the board.
